changelog: Replace C7 to explicitly treat cuts that end inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses or before a clause‑finishing verb that provides a qualification/reversal as very high contradiction risk — addresses the primary finding that contra is underestimated for such prefixes.

Replace C12 to allow, when dense (short‑chunk) segmentation is required, cuts immediately after determiners/short prepositions provided they do not separate a head from its required complements — addresses the finding that the prompt discouraged needed early cuts in short‑latency settings.

Replace C12 to allow cuts after determiners/short prepositions in dense (short‑chunk) settings when they do not detach a head from required complements — addresses the primary finding that the prompt was too conservative and lost short‑latency gains.

Insert after C7 a new principle that treats cuts ending inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses (before the clause‑finishing verb that supplies a qualification/reversal) as very high contra risk — addresses the finding that contra was underestimated for unfinished subordinate/verb‑final clauses.
Replace E1 with labeled example de_de_86 to teach the model that cuts ending inside subordinate/verb-final clauses (before the clause-finishing verb/qualification) carry very high contradiction risk.
Replace E2 with labeled example de_de_587 to expose short-latency cases where early cuts after function words may be acceptable and to show trade-offs for dense segmentation.

Replace E3 with labeled example de_de_240 to add a measured short/medium example that illustrates fragmentation after determiners/prepositions and helps the model learn when such cuts are harmful versus acceptable.

Replace C7 to explicitly mark cuts that end inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses (before the clause‑finishing verb or qualifying phrase) as high contradiction risk, addressing the finding that contra was underestimated for such prefixes.

Replace C12 to relax the rule for determiners/short prepositions in dense (short‑chunk) settings: allow cuts after them when they do not detach a head noun or required complements, addressing the finding that the prompt was too conservative and lost short‑latency gains.
